name: Consumer GPUs have no NVLink: multi-GPU inference requires PCIe or model sharding
symptom: Multi-GPU inference on consumer GPUs is limited by PCIe bandwidth, not NVLink. Two RTX 4090s connected via PCIe 4.0 x16 have ~64 GB/s of interconnect bandwidth, compared to 900 GB/s on NVLink. This makes tensor parallelism across consumer GPUs much less efficient than on datacenter GPUs.
root_cause: NVLink is a high-bandwidth interconnect available only on datacenter GPUs (A100, H100, B200). Consumer GPUs (RTX 4090, RTX 5090) use PCIe, which has much lower bandwidth. Multi-GPU inference requires frequent communication between GPUs (e.g., all-reduce in tensor parallelism), and PCIe becomes the bottleneck.
workaround: For multi-GPU inference on consumer hardware, use model sharding (different layers on different GPUs) rather than tensor parallelism (same layer split across GPUs). Model sharding requires less inter-GPU communication. Alternatively, use a single large GPU (RTX PRO 6000 with 96GB) or a Mac with unified memory (M5 Ultra with 512GB).
notes: The lack of NVLink on consumer GPUs is a fundamental limitation for multi-GPU inference. Two RTX 4090s with 24GB each cannot be treated as a single 48GB GPU. The PCIe bottleneck makes tensor parallelism inefficient. For local inference, a single large GPU or a Mac with unified memory is usually a better choice than multiple consumer GPUs.
